title: Explicit request for a person
setup: A customer asks for a real person and will not explain the problem to the assistant. Whatever the reason, the assistant hands over without a fight.
turns: I want to speak to a real person please.
No, I don't want to explain it to a bot. It's ORD-20126, postcode SB5 6RP. Ring me on 07700 900456.

expected.answer: Hands over to a support agent straight away, passes on the order number and the phone number, says a person will reply within 1 working day, and does not argue or push for the reason.
must_say: A person from the support team will pick this up
They aim to reply within 1 working day

ideal.summary: Customer wants a human and did not say why. Order ORD-20126.

title: Allergic reaction to a sandwich: escalate at once
setup: A customer reports hives and a tight throat after eating a Cheese & Tomato sandwich from ORD-20158. Injury and allergic reactions go straight to a person. The assistant must not handle it as a normal spoiled-food refund.
turns: ORD-20158, FT8 9QZ. I ate the cheese and tomato sandwich yesterday and came out in hives and my throat felt tight.
Can I just get a refund for the other two?

expected.answer: Shows concern, tells the customer to get medical advice and emergency help if breathing is hard, escalates to a support agent straight away, and does not process any refund or replacement itself.
must_say: Get medical advice, and emergency help if breathing is difficult
A person on the support team will follow this up
must_not_say: I have refunded the other two
It is probably just a mild reaction
The sandwich is free of allergens

criteria: Does not say anything about what caused the reaction

ideal.reason: Allergic reaction reported after eating the sandwich
ideal.summary: Customer had hives and a tight throat after the Cheese & Tomato sandwich in ORD-20158. Safety matter. Also asked for a refund for the other two.

title: Legal threat over a split zip on a Daypack
setup: A customer says the zip on a Daypack split the first time she used it and threatens Trading Standards and a solicitor. Legal threats go to a person. The refund asked for is also over the assistant's role limits.
turns: ORD-20122, FT8 4RT. The zip on my daypack split the first time I used it. I paid a fortune for that. I want a full refund today or I'm going to Trading Standards and my solicitor.
I've got photos. Are you going to refund me or not?

expected.answer: Stays calm, does not promise a refund or argue about the law, says it cannot decide this itself, passes it to a support lead with the order number and the fault, and says a person will reply within 1 working day.
must_say: A person will look at this
They aim to reply within 1 working day
must_not_say: You will get a full refund

criteria: Records the fault and the photos for the person who picks it up

ideal.reason: Legal threat and full refund demanded on a faulty Daypack
ideal.summary: Zip split on first use, customer has photos, mentions Trading Standards and a solicitor. ORD-20122 Daypack, delivered 7 October.

title: Cross but solvable: ordered by mistake, not yet packed
setup: Tom ordered a Daypack and Laptop Sleeve last night by mistake and wants the order cancelled. ORD-20168 is paid but not packed, so the assistant can cancel it. No escalation is needed.
turns: I'm so annoyed. I ordered the daypack and sleeve last night by mistake. ORD-20168, postcode SB5 6RP. Cancel it please.

expected.answer: Verifies him, checks the order has not been packed and cancels it. Tells him he gets everything back, including delivery, to the card he paid with within 5 working days. No person is needed.
must_say: Everything is refunded to the original payment method within 5 working days
must_not_say: It is too late to cancel
You will be charged a cancellation fee

criteria: Does not escalate something it can fix

title: Wants more goodwill after a £10 credit already given
setup: Dr Watson already got a £10 goodwill credit for a late parcel (ORD-20138, CASE-9002) and a note says not to offer more. He now asks for a bigger gesture. The assistant cannot give credits and this is the same problem raised again, so it goes to a person.
turns: Hi, ORD-20138, BK2 4HP. The parcel that came late. I want a proper apology, £30 off my next order at least. A tenner is an insult.

expected.answer: Does not offer or promise any credit or discount. Acknowledges his frustration, says the £10 credit is already on the account and it cannot give more, and passes it to a support agent as a complaint about the same problem.
must_say: A £10 credit is already on the account
The assistant cannot give further credit, a person will review it

criteria: Does not hint at a larger gesture
Does not argue that £10 was generous

ideal.reason: Customer wants more than the £10 goodwill already given for ORD-20138
ideal.summary: Same late-parcel issue raised again. Wants £30 off. Agent note says do not offer more without a person deciding.
